title: Carpenter Salary Australia: Award Rates, Annual Pay, and Tax in 2026
description: Find the carpenter salary Australia based on the Building and Construction Award. See hourly rates, annual pay for 38 hours, casual loading, tax, and super.
salarySummary: A full-time weekly hire carpenter on the Building and Construction Award earns about $63,825 per year (38 hours/week) before tax, based on the Level 3 rate plus allowances.

faqs.q: What is the average carpenter salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026), which is about $108,352 per year. However, the award minimum for a carpenter (Level 3) is lower. Many carpenters earn above award through experience, overtime, or enterprise agreements. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more comparisons.

faqs.q: How is super calculated for a carpenter?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a carpenter earning $63,825, that adds about $7,659 per year. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for details.

faqs.q: Does the award rate include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The award minimum rates are for permanent employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the ordinary hourly rate. For example, a casual carpenter at Level 3 would earn about $40.38 per hour (including allowances). Learn more on our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Carpenter Salary Australia Landscape

When you search for "carpenter salary australia", the figures you find can vary widely depending on whether they come from award minimums, industry surveys, or official statistics. This article uses the most authoritative source: the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Building and Construction General On-site Award 2020 (MA000020), updated to 1 July 2026. We’ll walk through how the award sets pay, how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary, and what tax and super mean for your take-home pay.

## How the Award Sets the Base Rate

The Building and Construction Award covers most on-site carpenters, joiners, and related trades. It classifies workers into levels (CW/ECW 1 to 9). A typical carpenter is classified at Level 3 (CW/ECW 3) or Level 4 depending on skill and experience. For Level 3, the minimum weekly rate is $1,119.10, which gives an hourly rate of $29.45. But that’s not the full story.

Carpenters are entitled to an industry allowance of $67.15 per week (clause 22) and, if they provide their own tools, a tool allowance of $41.22 per week (clause 21.1). These allowances are part of the ordinary hourly rate for all purposes.

For a **weekly hire** employee, the ordinary hourly rate is calculated as:

(minimum weekly rate + industry allowance + tool allowance) ÷ 38

= ($1,119.10 + $67.15 + $41.22) ÷ 38 = $1,227.47 ÷ 38 = **$32.30 per hour**

For a **daily hire** employee (common in construction), the award applies a factor of 52/50.4 to account for time between jobs. The daily hire ordinary hourly rate becomes:

$1,227.47 × (52 ÷ 50.4) ÷ 38 ≈ $33.32 per hour

These are the minimum rates. Many carpenters earn above award through experience, specialisation, or enterprise agreements.

## From Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week Assumption

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume 38 ordinary hours per week for a full-time employee, as defined in the award. Using the weekly hire carpenter rate:

$32.30 × 38 × 52 = **$63,824.80 per year**

For a daily hire carpenter:

$33.32 × 38 × 52 = **$65,840.32 per year**

If you work more than 38 hours, overtime rates apply (usually 150% or 200%), which would increase annual earnings. But for a baseline salary comparison, the 38-hour week is the standard.

## Casual Loading and What It Means

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the ordinary hourly rate in lieu of paid leave and other entitlements. For a casual carpenter (weekly hire base):

$32.30 × 1.25 = **$40.38 per hour**

If a casual worked a consistent 38 hours per week (unlikely, but for comparison), annual gross would be:

$40.38 × 38 × 52 = **$79,790.88**

However, casuals don’t get annual leave, sick leave, or public holiday pay. The loading compensates for that. Learn more on our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

## Comparing with National Benchmarks

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). The casual rate is $33.05 per hour (including 25% loading). The carpenter award rates are significantly higher, reflecting the skill and conditions of the trade.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 per year. The carpenter award minimum is below that average, but many carpenters with experience or in specialised roles earn above the award. For more context, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners).

For a weekly hire carpenter earning $63,825:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: $26,800 × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$63,825: $18,825 × 30% = $5,647.50
- Total tax: $9,667.50
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,276.50
- **Total deductions: $10,944**
- **Estimated take-home pay: $52,881 per year**

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For this carpenter, that’s an extra $7,659 per year contributed to super. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) pages for more details.

## Fortnightly Pay for Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a weekly hire carpenter:
- Weekly: $1,227.47
- Fortnightly: $1,227.47 × 2 = **$2,494.94**

For a daily hire carpenter:
- Weekly: $1,266.14
- Fortnightly: **$2,532.28**

Using our [the timesheet](/) tool, you can enter your own hourly rate and see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures instantly.

## Using the Pay Guides and Reference Tables

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award, including the Building and Construction Award. These guides list all minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can access them via our [pay guides](/blog) page. For detailed classification definitions and allowance tables, see our [reference tables](/data).

Remember: the figures here are estimates based on award minimums and standard assumptions. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, allowances, enterprise agreements, or individual contracts. Always check your pay against the award or your agreement.
